messages:
amy: Hey team — `py-ts` canary publish failed hitting PyPI with 401s. Deploy bot posted failure, npm publish looked fine. Any quick triage before we decide rollforward vs revert?

deploy-bot: [deploy] publish-job #4321 failed: twine upload exited 1 (HTTPError 401 Unauthorized) — logs: https://ci/internal/4321/logs
jordan: Ugh. Was this from the runner secrets rotation last night? I saw a KMS rotation event for the pypi key.
pat: Confirmed: npm registry used the OAuth app token (still valid). PyPI token expired/rotated and didn't get the new secret in runner.
sean: If consumers use soft-pins (>=) we can republish a fixed wheel and keep canary tag. If they pin exact wheels we need to roll back. Do we know how many customers are pinned?
marta: Quick check — our telemetry shows 3 known enterprise customers with exact-pins to `v1.8.2-canary.3` wheels (by filename). Others use >= constraints.
jordan: OK decision call: we prefer roll-forward if we can republish quickly with the same version metadata, otherwise revert the canary tag and yank the bad artifact. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
pat: We cannot re-use the same wheel filename on PyPI for a different file. Options: (1) revoke bad artifact and publish a patched build with `+rev1` local version suffix, (2) yank release and re-run full publish after secret fix. (3) create a transient `canary-temp` tag and coordinate consumers.
amy: Timebox 30m. Sean and Pat you take creds rotation + republish options. Jordan to decide rollback if not resolved in 30m. I'll notify customer success.
pat: Triage steps I'm running now: 1) validate secrets in vault 2) create ephemeral PyPI token scope to upload 3) republish to test index (test.pypi.org) to validate upload flow. Commands I'm testing: ```bash
# create/validate token (internal CLI)
secretsctl fetch pypi/uploader --env canary
# replicate upload locally
twine upload -r testpypi dist/* --verbose
```
sean: If we go ephemeral token route, we must rotate it out and audit. I'll prepare the revocation playbook and a short note for security and compliance.
jordan: Also we need to update release notes that this canary was reissued due to credential expiry and include checksum of the new wheel. docs-bot: reminder: run `./scripts/generate_release_notes --canary` after publish to auto-insert checksums.
amy: Status update — ephemeral token created, upload to test.pypi succeeded. Pushing to main PyPI in 2m. Will use `v1.8.2-canary.3+rev1` as the artifact tag to avoid filename collision.
pat: Command used: ```bash
PYPI_TOKEN=*** twine upload dist/*.whl --repository pypi
# then tag npm side unchanged
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.8.2-canary.3 canary
```
marta: Alerting the 3 exact-pin customers privately that we'll provide a patched wheel and recommend switching to soft-pins to avoid future churn.
jordan: After publish, ops: - mark old wheel yanked on PyPI - post short deprecation note in release notes explaining `+rev1` suffix and why. - set follow-up task to ensure secrets pipeline picks up KMS rotation.
amy: Publish complete — PyPI upload succeeded, checksums: sha256:abc123... New artifact `1.8.2-canary.3+rev1` available. Verified basic smoke tests local. :shipit:
sean: Revoking ephemeral token now and filing rotation ticket (#R-789).
pat: Yanked the bad artifact and added a README snippet in the canary bucket pointing to the new artifact. Also added a soft-pin recommendation to the deprecation section.
jordan: Closing the decision: roll-forward via republish with `+rev1`, no revert. We've created followup tasks: secrets sync, customer outreach, release notes update. Thanks all. :tada:
docs-bot: release-notes updated: https://docs.internal/releases/1.8.2-canary.3-rev1.html
amy: I'll draft a short post to #customers and update the changelog entry. Good job moving fast.
